terms.title: Gini coefficient
terms.definition: The Gini coefficient measures how unevenly income or spending is shared, from 0 (everyone has the same amount) to 1 (one person has it all). In a made-up example, 0.6 means more inequality than 0.2.

terms.title: Market exchange rate
terms.definition: A market exchange rate is the price of one currency in another. For example, at a made-up rate of $1 for 5 pesos, 100 pesos is worth $20.

terms.title: CRISPR
terms.definition: CRISPR is a tool scientists use to make targeted changes to DNA, the instruction code inside cells. Think of it as finding a chosen line in a long instruction book and editing it.

terms.title: Genome
terms.definition: A genome is a living thing’s complete set of DNA instructions. Sequencing a genome means reading the order of the letters in that code.

terms.title: Gene editing
terms.definition: Gene editing means making a chosen change to DNA, the instruction code inside cells. Scientists can add, remove or replace parts of that code to study how it works or try to treat disease.

terms.title: Genes
terms.definition: Genes are sections of DNA that carry instructions for making molecules a cell uses. Some tell cells how to make proteins; others make RNA molecules that do jobs of their own.
